Packaging Printing Methods Compared: Offset, Digital, Flexo and Gravure

Published August 26, 2026 · Buyer guide · By BestPackFactory

Quick answer

Choose the print method by quantity, color complexity and lead time: offset suits medium runs with fine detail on board, digital suits short runs and variable data, flexo suits flexible film and labels at volume, and gravure suits very long runs with premium detail. Ask suppliers to quote the same job on the methods they offer.

Decision table

MethodBest run lengthStrengths
OffsetMedium to longFine detail, cost at volume
DigitalShort, variable dataFast, no plates
FlexoLong, film and labelsSpeed on flexible packaging
GravureVery longPremium detail and consistency

Run length decides the method

Digital shines below a few thousand pieces; offset becomes efficient at medium runs; flexo and gravure amortize setup costs over long runs. Compare total cost including setup, plates or cylinders at your quantity.

Color quality and substrates

Offset and gravure deliver the finest detail; flexo quality varies by press and prepress. Confirm the substrate (board, film, label stock) works with the method and that lamination or coating does not change the final color.

Variable data and personalization

Digital printing enables variable data such as unique codes, names or seasonal variations without plates. If your program needs personalization, digital is the practical choice.

Ask for a method-agnostic quote

Ask the supplier to quote the same job on the methods they offer, including setup, plates or cylinders, proofs and lead time. The cheapest per-unit price at your volume may not be the cheapest total.

Buyer checklist

  1. Compare total cost at your volume
  2. Match method to substrate
  3. Check color quality expectations
  4. Consider variable data needs
  5. Include setup and proof costs

Frequently asked questions

Which method is cheapest for small orders?

Digital typically wins at short runs because there are no plates or cylinders; compare quotes at your quantity.

Can flexo match offset quality?

Modern flexo is close on many jobs, but offset and gravure still lead on the finest detail; evaluate with proofs.

Do I need gravure for premium boxes?

Only at very large volumes; offset or high-quality flexo usually meets premium expectations at lower setup cost.

What the Spec Means for Buyers

Printing method choice maps to volume and structure. Offset suits folding cartons and boxes at 1–8 colors with the highest fidelity (ΔE ≤ 3.0); digital covers short runs and variable data; flexo handles corrugated at 1–4 colors; gravure is the high-volume flexible-packaging standard at ±0.3 mm registration. The factory applies offset, flexo or digital to paper structures and gravure or digital to films, with CMYK + Pantone matching. MOQ is 500 PCS per size and artwork.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which method gives the highest print fidelity?

Offset printing at 175 LPI with CTP plates gives the highest fidelity for paper packaging.

Which method suits flexible film?

Gravure is the high-volume film standard; digital covers short-run and variable-data film jobs.
